applicability: validated on-disk record stores with an exact-field reader; excludes append-only logs and stores with no schema validation

evidence.source_reference: PR #116 e8f0205 scripts/learning_ledger.py (implementation); ledger population read at ad0f17e (26 singular retest blocks, 11 of them pass)

expected_behavior: A record-shape change states its migration decision explicitly -- one-shot, version-gated, or a permanent compatibility reader with its dual-form cost accepted -- and says what rollback does to a record that already moved.
observation: A ledger rework changed record shape and migrated on first write. A normalizing reader kept both shapes readable, so nothing broke -- but that reader was an implementation detail rather than a stated choice, and two consequences rode in unchosen. Convergence is unguaranteed rather than automatic: the retest path refuses a settled pass, so those records move only if a later release cycle happens to archive them, which may never occur. And rollback silently changed meaning -- stripping the new key from an already-migrated record also deletes the attempt the old shape held.
reason: Traced in the reverted implementation: the reader normalizes both shapes and a later release cycle does migrate a settled record, so neither readability nor convergence is impossible. What is missing is the decision and its rollback statement, not a forced migration.
